gaps.sentence: The scheme is costly; on the ___ hand, it would create hundreds of jobs.
gaps.explanation: 'On the other hand' balances a drawback against an advantage.

gaps.sentence: ___ the heavy rain, the match went ahead.
gaps.explanation: 'Despite' takes a noun phrase; 'although' needs a clause.

gaps.sentence: ___ the strike, trains will run a reduced service all week.
gaps.explanation: 'Because of the strike' gives the reason for the reduced service.

gaps.sentence: The ferry was cancelled; ___, we drove the long way round.
gaps.explanation: 'Consequently' introduces the consequence of the cancellation.

gaps.sentence: It sounds ___ the negotiations are close to a breakthrough.
gaps.explanation: 'It sounds as though...' reports an impression.

gaps.sentence: I enjoyed the film; the ending was weak, ___.
gaps.explanation: 'Though' can come at the end of a sentence as a casual contrast marker; the others cannot.

gaps.sentence: Far from resenting the changes, the staff welcomed them; ___, productivity rose.
gaps.explanation: Rising productivity is an additional point in the same direction: moreover.
'Firstly' opens a sequence of instructions; eventually/finally close one.
